text: The flashcard design's first attempt put `review(Grade, int)` on `Card`. What signaled that this was wrong?
choices: Grades are an enum, and enums may not be passed to methods on immutable types.
The method needed the scheduling policy, a collaborator the card has no business knowing about.
The method mutated the card, which would have made it unusable as a map key.
`Card` was a record, and records may not declare methods that use their components.
explanation: Either every card carries a reference to the same scheduler, or `review` takes one as a parameter — in which case the caller must know about scheduling, which is the thing the design was trying to encapsulate. Needing a collaborator to do its own job is the signal that a responsibility has been written on the wrong card. The second attempt, `LeitnerCard extends Card`, failed differently: a policy is not a kind of card, and the choice needed to be made at run time.
